cards.explanation: The answer is wilderness. Luke 3:2 says the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness. Tiberius, Pilate, Herod, Annas and Caiaphas are all named, and the word of God comes to John.

The answer is repentance. John preaches “…a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins…” (Luke 3:3). Repentance means turning away from sin and turning back to God, and forgiveness of sins goes with it. John also tells the crowds to produce fruit in keeping with repentance (Luke 3:8).

The answer is for the Lord. The voice cries, "Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him." (Luke 3:4). The road work is all for Him, friends. Somebody important is coming, and I think that's why the whole job site is so serious.

The answer is False. Luke 3:5 says, "The crooked ways shall be made straight, and the rough ways smooth." Valleys, hills, crooked ways, and rough ways all get changed. Even I can't leave a bent cookie alone, and I'm just a stamper.
The answer is "You brood of vipers." John says, “You brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?” (Luke 3:7). He says it to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, friends.

The answer is "We have Abraham as our father." John says, “And do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’…” (Luke 3:8). Having the right family name doesn't replace fruit, bakers. It's like saying my stamper is famous, so my cookies don't need to come out right.

The answer is True. John says, "For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham." (Luke 3:8). Stones, of all things, friends. If God can do that, I think the crowd can stop leaning on their family tree.

The answer is that it will be cut down and thrown into the fire. John says, “…every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.” (Luke 3:9). The axe lies ready at the root, friends. That's the picture John gives the crowds.

The answer is share. John says, "Whoever has two tunics should share with him who has none…" (Luke 3:11). A tunic was a piece of clothing, and the second one goes to the person with none. Simple, and nobody needs a committee.

The answer is True. John says, “…and whoever has food should do the same.” (Luke 3:11). Whoever has two tunics shares with him who has none, and whoever has food does the same. The tunics and the food get the same instruction, friends.

The answer is to collect no more than they're authorized. John answers the tax collectors, "Collect no more than you are authorized…" (Luke 3:13). Do the job, and take only what you're allowed, friends. I think that's a clear answer.

The answers are content and wages. John tells the soldiers, "Be content with your wages." (Luke 3:14). Content means being okay with what you're paid. A good word for any payday. Wages are what they're paid for the work, and John points them right back to that pay.

The answer is if John could be the Christ. Luke 3:15 says the people “…were all wondering in their hearts if John could be the Christ.” The verse says they were waiting expectantly, friends. John's about to answer them straight.

The answer is not worthy to untie His sandal straps. John says of the One coming, "…the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie." (Luke 3:16). He puts himself below even that small job, friends. That's about as humble as it gets.

The answer is False. John says, "…to gather the wheat into His barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire." (Luke 3:17). Wheat in the barn, chaff burned. It's a hard picture, friends, and I think that's how John meant it.

The answer is that he locks John up in prison. Luke 3:20 says, "He locked John up in prison." It's a heavy moment, friends, and I think this one hurts. John said what was true, and Herod added this to everything else he had done.
